from.place: proof of Tag 0BF3: Kunneth injectivity for H^1 of the special fibre product

title: Kunneth injectivity for the first cohomology of a product
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $X$ and $Y$ be proper schemes over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-scheme-over-base] with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$ and $H^0(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=k$. For $k$-rational points [def-pc-rational-point] $x\in X(k)$ and $y\in Y(k)$, the homomorphism $H^1(X \times_k Y,\mathcal O_{X \times_k Y}) \to H^1(X,\mathcal O_X) \oplus H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ given by pullback along the slices $(1,y):X\to X\times_kY$ and $(x,1):Y\to X\times_kY$ is injective.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma varieties-lemma-kunneth, Tag 0BED, applied in degree 1 to O_X and O_Y

proof.text: By pqf-lem-proper-basic applied to the proper structure morphisms X→Spec(k) and Y→Spec(k) (with affine base Spec(k)), X and Y are quasi-compact and separated. Separatedness means the diagonals are closed immersions, and closed immersions are affine morphisms, so X and Y have affine diagonals. Thus the hypotheses of lem-sc-picard-kunneth-qcoh apply to the structure sheaves.

Specializing the Kunneth isomorphism to F=O_X, G=O_Y and n=1 gives H^1(X ×_{Spec(k)} Y,O) ≅ (H^1(X,O) ⊗_k H^0(Y,O)) ⊕ (H^0(X,O) ⊗_k H^1(Y,O)), since the only pairs of nonnegative degrees summing to 1 are (1,0) and (0,1). Using H^0(X,O)=k=H^0(Y,O), this identifies H^1(X ×_{Spec(k)} Y,O) with H^1(X,O) ⊕ H^1(Y,O).

source.place: Varieties, Lemma varieties-lemma-kunneth, Tag 0BED, degree n=1

proof.text: Under this decomposition, the functoriality of the canonical cup-product map in lem-sc-picard-kunneth-qcoh shows that pullback along the slice (1,y):X→X×_{Spec(k)}Y is the identity on the H^1(X,O) summand, because pr_1∘(1,y)=id_X and pr_2^*1=1, and is zero on the H^1(Y,O) summand, because pr_2∘(1,y) factors as X→Spec(k)→Y through the k-rational point y [def-pc-rational-point], so its pullback on H^1 factors through H^1(Spec(k),O_{Spec(k)}), which is 0 by pqf-lem-affine-vanishing (Spec(k) is affine). Similarly, pullback along (x,1):Y→X×_{Spec(k)}Y is zero on the first summand and the identity on the second.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma varieties-lemma-kunneth, Tag 0BED, proof description of the cup-product maps and functoriality

proof.text: Therefore the homomorphism obtained by the two slice pullbacks is the identity map on H^1(X,O)⊕H^1(Y,O) after the displayed identification, and is consequently injective.

source.place: Varieties, Lemma varieties-lemma-kunneth, Tag 0BED, degree n=1

lean.statement: theorem picard_h1_product_injective (k : Type u) [Field k] (X Y : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsProper (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsProper (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] (hX : Function.Bijective (globalSectionsRingHom k (X := X))) (hY : Function.Bijective (globalSectionsRingHom k (X := Y))) (x : (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).fieldPoints k) (y : (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).fieldPoints k) : let f := X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k) let g := Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k) let iX : X ⟶ pullback f g := pullback.lift (𝟙 X) (f ≫ y.1) (by dsimp only [f, g] rw [Category.id_comp, Category.assoc, y.2] simp) let iY : Y ⟶ pullback f g := pullback.lift (g ≫ x.1) (𝟙 Y) (by dsimp only [f, g] rw [Category.id_comp, Category.assoc, x.2] simp) Function.Injective ((structureSheafCohomologyPullback iX 1).prod (structureSheafCohomologyPullback iY 1))

reviewed_lean.note: k Field; X,Y Over Spec k with IsProper on X↘/Y↘; H0=k as bijective globalSectionsRingHom; x,y fieldPoints (sections); X×_kY = pullback f g; iX=lift(𝟙,f≫y), iY=lift(g≫x,𝟙) = (1,y),(x,1); H1 = Sheaf.H of O_ab on Zariski site, pullback = Ext map via exact f^{-1}, ℤ comparison, adjoint of f.c; conclusion Injective of AddMonoidHom.prod
